units.title: Living together in peace
units.notes: Peace means living without fighting. We play and share happily with others. We respect everyone, young and old. We solve problems by talking kindly. We say sorry when we do wrong. Peace makes our community happy. We do not fight or shout at each other. We help to keep our home and school calm. God wants us to live in peace. A peaceful home is a happy home.
units.worked_example: Talk about two friends who disagreed over a toy. Show how they talked and shared instead of fighting.
units.activity: Say one kind word to each friend in your group and give a gentle handshake.
units.check: What can you do to keep peace at home and school?

quiz.prompt: What does peace mean?
How should we solve problems?
We should respect everyone, young and old?
What should we do when we do wrong?
A peaceful home is a sad home?

English.overview: A simple guide to early English for Grades 1 to 3, covering letter sounds, reading short words, and writing clear sentences. It builds step by step from sounds to complete sentences using everyday Kenyan examples.

units.title: Letter sounds and names
units.notes: Letters have both a name and a sound, and we say the sound of a letter when we read words. For example, the letter b makes the sound we hear at the start of ball, bag and baby, while the letter s starts sun, sack and school. We should practise saying each sound slowly and clearly every day. Knowing letter sounds well helps you to read many new words by yourself with confidence.
units.worked_example: Say the sound of the first letter in each of these words: mat, sun and hat. The answers are m, s and h.
units.activity: Walk around your home and find three things that start with the sound s, then say each name aloud to a friend.
units.check: What sound does the first letter of the word market make?

quiz.prompt: Which letter sound do we hear at the start of ball, bag and baby?
Every letter has both a name and a sound.
The letter s makes the sound we hear at the start of which word?
How often should we practise saying letter sounds?
Knowing letter sounds well helps you read new words by yourself.

units.title: Joining sounds to make words
units.notes: When we blend, we say letter sounds quickly and join them to make one word. For example, c-a-t makes cat, m-a-t makes mat and b-a-g makes bag. Blending is like stretching a rubber band and then letting it snap back into one word. Practise blending sounds for a few minutes every day, and soon you will read many short words without any help. This makes your reading smooth, quick and easy.
units.worked_example: Blend these sounds aloud: m-a-t. They join to make the word mat. Now try s-u-n to make sun.
units.activity: Write five short words on small cards, cut them into separate sounds, then join the sounds again to read each word.
units.check: Which word do the sounds h-o-p make?

quiz.prompt: Which word do the sounds c-a-t make?
The sounds m-a-t make which word?
Blending means saying letter sounds quickly and joining them to make one word.
What is blending compared to in the notes?
Practising blending helps you read short words without help.

units.title: Reading and writing short words
units.notes: Many short words have three sounds, one at the start, one in the middle and one at the end. We call them CVC words because they are a consonant, a vowel and a consonant. Examples are pen, bag, cup and sit. Reading and writing these words every day makes you a strong reader. Try to spell each word as you say its sounds.
units.worked_example: The sounds b-e-d come together to make bed. Write the word bed in your book and read it back to yourself.
units.activity: Look at pictures in a book and write the three-letter word that names each picture, such as cat, dog or cup.
units.check: Can you write the word cup by saying its three sounds?

quiz.prompt: A CVC word is made of a consonant, a vowel and what else?
Which word is a CVC word?
CVC words have three sounds, one at the start, one in the middle and one at the end.
Which of these are CVC words?
Writing short words every day makes you a strong reader.

units.title: Common words we see often
units.notes: Some words appear again and again in what we read. We call them sight words because we learn to know them at once. Words like the, and, is, my and you are sight words. We do not sound them out slowly, we read them quickly. Learning sight words helps your reading to become smooth and fast, so read them every day.
units.worked_example: Read this sentence quickly: The boy is my friend. Point to each sight word as you read it.
units.activity: Make a list of five sight words and read them aloud to a family member three times today.
units.check: Can you spot and read the word you in a story book?

quiz.prompt: What do we call words like the, and, is, my and you that we learn to know at once?
We sound out sight words slowly letter by letter.
Which of these is a sight word?
How should we read sight words?
Learning sight words helps reading to become smooth and fast.

units.title: Reading simple sentences
units.notes: A sentence is a group of words that tells a complete idea. It begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. A simple sentence like The goat eats grass tells us who does something and what happens. Read slowly and point to each word as you go, because this helps you to understand what you read, and it makes reading fun.
units.worked_example: Read this sentence: The girl washes her hands. The girl is who the sentence is about, and washing her hands is what she does.
units.activity: Read three short sentences from a book to a friend, then tell them what each sentence means.
units.check: What mark do we put at the end of a telling sentence?

quiz.prompt: What does a telling sentence begin with?
What mark do we put at the end of a telling sentence?
A sentence is a group of words that tells a complete idea.
Which of these is a complete sentence?
Pointing to each word as you read helps you understand what you read.

units.title: Capital letters and full stops
units.notes: Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. We also use capital letters for names of people, towns and the word I. For example, Amina lives in Nakuru begins with a capital A. Writing with capital letters and full stops makes your work very clear and easy to read. Always check your sentences carefully for both capital letters and full stops.
units.worked_example: Fix this sentence: my name is juma. The correct sentence is: My name is Juma.
units.activity: Copy three sentences from your reading book and circle every capital letter and full stop that you find.
units.check: Where should the capital letter go in the sentence we live in kisumu?

quiz.prompt: Every sentence starts with what?
Which words should also begin with a capital letter?
We use a capital letter for the word I.
In the sentence we live in kisumu, which word needs a capital letter?
Writing with capital letters and full stops makes your work clear.

units.title: Naming words: nouns
units.notes: Nouns are naming words. They name people, places, animals and things, and they answer the question of who or what a thing is. In the sentence Kiptoo has a new bag, Kiptoo and bag are nouns. There are nouns all around you in the classroom, home and market. Knowing nouns helps you to talk and write about the world clearly.
units.worked_example: In the sentence The dog sleeps under the table, the nouns are dog and table.
units.activity: List five nouns you can see in your classroom right now, such as desk, door or window.
units.check: Which word in Mama cooks ugali is a noun?

quiz.prompt: Nouns are words that name what?
In the sentence Kiptoo has a new bag, which words are nouns?
Nouns answer the question of who or what a thing is.
In Mama cooks ugali, which word is a noun?
Knowing nouns helps you talk and write about the world clearly.

units.title: Doing words: verbs
units.notes: Verbs are doing words that tell us what someone or something does. In the sentence The baby cries, the word cries is a verb. Verbs can show many actions such as run, eat, sing, write, jump, dance and swim. Every complete sentence needs a doing word to make sense, so look carefully for the action to find the verb. Actions are all around you.
units.worked_example: Find the verb in The boys play football. The verb is play, because it tells us what the boys do.
units.activity: Act out five action words for a friend, such as hop, clap and skip, and ask them to name each action.
units.check: What is the doing word in the sentence The bird sings sweetly?

quiz.prompt: Verbs are words that tell us what?
In the sentence The baby cries, which word is the verb?
Every complete sentence needs a doing word to make sense.
Which of these words is a verb?
In the sentence The bird sings sweetly, the verb is sings.

units.title: Colour and number words
units.notes: We can write colours and numbers as words. Words like red, blue, yellow, green, one, two and three help us to describe things. For example, I have two red pencils uses both a number word and a colour word. Learning these words makes your writing much more interesting, clear and exact. Try using them when you describe the objects around you.
units.worked_example: Read and write the sentence: She has three blue pens. The number word is three and the colour word is blue.
units.activity: Choose five objects at home and write a short phrase for each one using a colour word and a number word.
units.check: How do you write the number 4 as a word?

quiz.prompt: Which words are colour words?
How do you write the number 4 as a word?
We can write colours and numbers as words.
In I have two red pencils, which is the number word?
Number and colour words make our writing more interesting and exact.

units.title: Days of the week
units.notes: A week has seven days in a special order. They are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. We go to school from Monday to Friday and rest on Saturday and Sunday. Knowing the days helps us to plan our work, keep appointments and remember events. We can write sentences such as We have games on Friday and We visit our grandmother on Sunday.
units.worked_example: If today is Wednesday, then tomorrow is Thursday and yesterday was Tuesday.
units.activity: Say the seven days of the week in order to a family member and tell them your favourite day.
units.check: Which day comes right after Sunday?

quiz.prompt: How many days are in a week?
Which day comes right after Sunday?
We go to school from Monday to Friday.
On which days do we rest at home?
Knowing the days of the week helps us plan our work.

units.title: Asking and answering questions
units.notes: Questions are the words we use when we want to know something. A question often begins with words like what, where, who, when, why or how. It always ends with a question mark. For example, the question Where is my bag asks about a place. Answering questions clearly shows that we understand what we read and hear every day at school.
units.worked_example: Question: Who is your teacher? A clear answer is: My teacher is Mr Otieno.
units.activity: Ask a friend three questions using what, where and who, and listen carefully to their answers.
units.check: What punctuation mark do we put at the end of a question?

quiz.prompt: What mark do we put at the end of a question?
Which word can begin a question?
A question always ends with a question mark.
The question Where is my bag asks about what?
Answering questions clearly shows that we understand what we read.

units.title: Telling and retelling stories
units.notes: Stories have a clear beginning, a middle and an end. When we retell a story, we tell what happened in the right order of time. We can use words like first, then, next and finally to show the order clearly. Listening to stories every day builds our vocabulary, our memory and our imagination. Retelling shows that we understood and remembered the story well.
units.worked_example: Retell a short story in order: First the hare ran fast. Then the tortoise walked slowly. Finally the tortoise won the race.
units.activity: Listen to a short story from a family member, then retell it to another person in your own words.
units.check: What three words can help you show the order of events in a story?

quiz.prompt: What three parts does a story have?
options: A title, a page and a cover
A beginning, a middle and an end
A pen, a book and a desk
A morning, a noon and a night

quiz.prompt: Which words help show the order of events in a story?
When we retell a story, we tell what happened in the right order.
Listening to stories every day helps build what?
Retelling shows that we understood and remembered the story.

units.title: Writing a short paragraph
units.notes: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one idea. Each sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. In Grade Three we can write three or four sentences about a topic we know well. For example, we can write about our school, our family or our pet. Writing every day makes our handwriting and spelling better.
units.worked_example: Write about your family: I live with my family in Thika. My father is a farmer. My mother sells vegetables. Each sentence is complete.
units.activity: Write four short sentences about your best friend and read them aloud to your class.
units.check: How many sentences should a short paragraph in your class have?

quiz.prompt: A paragraph is a group of sentences about what?
How many sentences can a Grade Three short paragraph have?
Each sentence in a paragraph begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
Which topics can we write about in a short paragraph?
options: Our school, our family or our pet

quiz.prompt: Writing every day makes our handwriting and spelling better.

Kiswahili.overview: Mwongozo huu rahisi wa Kiswahili kwa Gredi ya Kwanza hadi ya Tatu unashughulikia sauti za herufi, kusoma maneno mafupi na kuandika sentensi wazi. Unajengwa hatua kwa hatua kuanzia sauti hadi sentensi kamili, ukitumia mifano ya kila siku ya Kenya.

units.title: Sauti za herufi
units.notes: Herufi zina jina na sauti, na tunatumia sauti ya herufi tunaposoma maneno. Kwa mfano, herufi b ina sauti tunayoisikia mwanzoni mwa neno baba, bakuli na benki, na herufi m inaanza mama, maji na mkate. Jizoeze kutamka kila sauti kwa polepole na kwa uwazi kila siku. Kujua sauti za herufi vizuri hukusaidia kusoma maneno mapya mwenyewe. Sauti hizi ni msingi wa kusoma na kuandika.
units.worked_example: Taja sauti ya herufi ya kwanza katika maneno haya: mama, kuku na shule. Majibu ni m, k na sh.
units.activity: Tembea nyumbani na utafute vitu vitatu vinavyoanza na sauti m, kisha vitaje kwa sauti kwa rafiki yako.
units.check: Sauti ya herufi ya kwanza ya neno soko ni ipi?

quiz.prompt: Sauti ya herufi ya kwanza ya neno baba, bakuli na benki ni ipi?
Herufi zina jina na sauti.
Herufi m inaanza maneno yapi?
Tunapaswa kutamka kila sauti vipi?
Kujua sauti za herufi hukusaidia kusoma maneno mapya.

units.title: Kuunganisha silabi
units.notes: Silabi ni sehemu ya neno inayotamkwa kwa mpigo mmoja tu. Tunapounganisha silabi mbili au tatu, tunapata neno kamili. Kwa mfano, silabi ba na ba zinaunganishwa kupata neno baba, na silabi ma na ji zinaunganishwa kupata neno maji. Kuunganisha silabi ni kama kushikilia vipande viwili vya ubao na kuvipachika pamoja kwa nguvu. Jizoeze kuunganisha silabi kila siku ili kusoma maneno kwa urahisi na kwa haraka.
units.worked_example: Unganisha silabi hizi kwa sauti: ma-ma. Zinaunda neno mama. Sasa jaribu ku-ku kupata kuku.
units.activity: Andika silabi za maneno matano kwenye karatasi, zitenganishe, kisha ziunganishe tena kusoma kila neno.
units.check: Silabi za neno sukari ni zipi?

quiz.prompt: Silabi ba na ba zinaunganishwa kupata neno gani?
Silabi ma na ji zinaunganishwa kupata neno gani?
Silabi ni sehemu ya neno inayotamkwa kwa mpigo mmoja.
Kuunganisha silabi kunafananishwa na nini?
options: Kushikilia vipande viwili vya ubao na kuvipachika pamoja

quiz.prompt: Kujizoeza kuunganisha silabi hufanya kusoma kuwa rahisi.

units.title: Maneno ya silabi mbili
units.notes: Maneno mengi mafupi yana silabi mbili, na tunayasoma kwa kuunganisha silabi zake pamoja. Mfano ni maneno kama moto, maji, mkate, kisu, chakula na kitabu. Tunayasoma kwa kuunganisha silabi zake mbili pamoja kwa sauti na kwa mpigo mmoja. Kuandika maneno haya mara kwa mara hufanya tusome na kuandika vizuri zaidi kila siku. Jaribu kutamka silabi moja moja kisha uzisome pamoja kwa haraka na kwa usahihi.
units.worked_example: Neno maji lina silabi ma na ji. Neno mkate lina silabi mka na te.
units.activity: Chora picha tatu na uandike neno la Kiswahili la silabi mbili chini ya kila picha.
units.check: Neno kisu lina silabi ngapi?

quiz.prompt: Neno kisu lina silabi ngapi?
Ni maneno yapi yana silabi mbili?
Maneno mengi mafupi yana silabi mbili.
Tunasoma maneno ya silabi mbili kwa kuunganisha nini?
Kuandika maneno haya mara kwa mara hufanya tusome na kuandika vizuri.

units.title: Maneno tunayoyaona mara nyingi
units.notes: Kuna maneno yanayojitokeza mara nyingi katika kusoma na kuandika, na tunayafahamu haraka bila kuyatamka kwa polepole. Mfano ni maneno kama na, ni, ya, wa, huyu, yule na wale. Kuyajua maneno haya hufanya kusoma kwetu kuwa rahisi na kwa haraka zaidi kila siku. Tusome maneno haya kila siku hadi tuyafahamu vyema bila kusita. Kuzijua maneno haya hutusaidia kuelewa sentensi haraka na kwa urahisi.
units.worked_example: Soma sentensi hii kwa haraka: Mtoto huyu ni rafiki yangu. Yaelekeze maneno unayoyafahamu haraka.
units.activity: Andika orodha ya maneno matano ya kawaida na uyasome kwa mzazi wako mara tatu leo.
units.check: Unaweza kusoma neno huyu bila kusita?

quiz.prompt: Tunafahamu maneno ya mara nyingi vipi?
Maneno kama na, ni, ya na wa tunayajua haraka.
Ni neno lipi tunaloyaona mara nyingi?
Kuyajua maneno haya hufanya kusoma kuwa vipi?
Tusome maneno haya kila siku hadi tuyafahamu vyema.

units.title: Kusoma sentensi fupi
units.notes: Sentensi ni kundi la maneno yanayotoa maana kamili kwa msomaji wake. Kila sentensi huanza na herufi kubwa na huisha na nukta mwishoni. Sentensi kama Mtoto anakula chakula hutueleza nani anafanya nini, wapi na wakati gani. Tunapaswa kusoma kwa polepole na kuelekeza kila neno tunaposoma kwa sauti ya wazi. Hii hukusaidia kuelewa vyema unachosoma na pia kusoma kwa haraka na kwa usahihi.
units.worked_example: Soma sentensi hii: Msichana anasafisha nyumba. Msichana ndiye anayehusika, na kusafisha nyumba ni kile anachofanya.
units.activity: Soma sentensi tatu fupi kutoka kitabu na umwambie rafiki yako maana ya kila sentensi.
units.check: Tunatumia alama gani mwishoni mwa sentensi inayoeleza?

quiz.prompt: Sentensi ni kundi la maneno yanayotoa nini?
Kila sentensi huanza na nini?
Sentensi huisha na nukta mwishoni.
Tunapaswa kusoma vipi?
options: Kwa polepole na kuelekeza kila neno

quiz.prompt: Kusoma kwa uangalifu hutusaidia kuelewa tunachosoma.

units.title: Herufi kubwa na nukta
units.notes: Kila sentensi huanza na herufi kubwa na huisha na nukta mwishoni. Tunatumia pia herufi kubwa kwa majina ya watu, miji, nchi na neno mimi. Kwa mfano, Amina anaishi Nakuru huanza na herufi kubwa A na mwisho nukta. Kuandika kwa herufi kubwa na nukta hufanya kazi yetu kuwa wazi na rahisi kusoma kila wakati. Angalia kila sentensi yako kwa mambo haya mawili kabla ya kuwasilisha kazi.
units.worked_example: Sahihisha sentensi hii: jina langu ni juma. Sentensi sahihi ni: Jina langu ni Juma.
units.activity: Nakili sentensi tatu kutoka kitabu chako na uzungushie kila herufi kubwa na nukta unayoiona.
units.check: Herufi kubwa inapaswa kuwa wapi katika sentensi tunaishi mombasa?

quiz.prompt: Kila sentensi huanza na nini?
Tunatumia herufi kubwa pia kwa nini?
options: Majina ya watu, miji na nchi

quiz.prompt: Tunatumia herufi kubwa kwa neno mimi.
Katika sentensi tunaishi mombasa, neno lipi linahitaji herufi kubwa?
Kuangalia sentensi kwa herufi kubwa na nukta hufanya kazi kuwa wazi.

units.title: Nomino: majina ya vitu
units.notes: Nomino ni maneno ya kuita majina ya watu na vitu. Hutaja watu, mahali, wanyama na vitu, na hujibu swali la nani au nini jambo ni. Katika sentensi Kiptoo ana mkoba mpya, Kiptoo na mkoba ni nomino mbili. Kuna nomino kila mahali karibu nawe kila siku: darasani, nyumbani, shambani na sokoni. Kujua nomino hukusaidia kuzungumza na kuandika kuhusu ulimwengu kwa uwazi na kwa ufasaha.
units.worked_example: Katika sentensi Mbwa analala chini ya meza, nomino ni mbwa na meza.
units.activity: Taja nomino tano unazoziona darasani sasa, kama dawati, mlango au dirisha.
units.check: Neno lipi katika Mama anapika ugali ni nomino?

quiz.prompt: Nomino ni maneno ya kuitaje nini?
Katika sentensi Kiptoo ana mkoba mpya, nomino ni zipi?
Nomino hujibu swali la nani au nini.
Katika Mama anapika ugali, neno lipi ni nomino?
Kujua nomino hukusaidia kuandika kuhusu ulimwengu kwa uwazi.

units.title: Vitenzi: maneno ya kutenda
units.notes: Vitenzi ni maneno ya kutenda yanayotueleza mtu au kitu anachofanya kila siku katika maisha. Katika sentensi kama Mtoto analia, neno analia ni kitenzi cha kutenda. Vitenzi huonyesha vitendo mbalimbali kama kukimbia, kula, kuimba, kuandika, kuruka, kucheza, kulima na kusoma. Kila sentensi kamili huhitaji kitenzi ili ikamilike na iwe na maana kamili kila wakati. Tafuta kitendo katika sentensi ili kupata kitenzi kwa urahisi.
units.worked_example: Tafuta kitenzi katika Wavulana wanacheza mpira. Kitenzi ni wanacheza, kwa sababu hutueleza wanachofanya.
units.activity: Igize vitendo vitano kwa rafiki yako, kama kuruka, kupiga makofi na kulima, na umwombe kutaja kila kitendo.
units.check: Kitenzi katika sentensi Ndege anaimba vizuri ni kipi?

quiz.prompt: Vitenzi ni maneno ya kutenda yanayotueleza nini?
Katika sentensi Mtoto analia, kitenzi ni kipi?
Kila sentensi kamili huhitaji kitenzi.
Ni neno lipi ni kitenzi?
Katika sentensi Ndege anaimba vizuri, kitenzi ni anaimba.

units.title: Rangi na namba kwa maneno
units.notes: Tunaweza kuandika rangi na namba kwa maneno badala ya kutumia tarakimu tu kila wakati. Maneno kama nyekundu, bluu, njano, kijani, moja, mbili, tatu na nne hutusaidia kuelezea vitu vyetu. Kwa mfano, sentensi Nina kalamu mbili nyekundu hutumia neno la namba na neno la rangi. Kujua maneno haya hufanya uandishi wetu kuwa wa kuvutia, wazi na sahihi. Jaribu kuyatumia unapoelezea vitu unavyoona nyumbani na shuleni.
units.worked_example: Soma na uandike sentensi: Ana kalamu tatu za bluu. Neno la namba ni tatu na neno la rangi ni bluu.
units.activity: Chagua vitu vitano nyumbani na uandike kifungu kifupi kwa kila kimoja ukitumia neno la rangi na la namba.
units.check: Namba 4 inaandikwaje kwa neno?

quiz.prompt: Maneno yapi ni maneno ya rangi?
Namba 4 inaandikwaje kwa neno?
Tunaweza kuandika rangi na namba kwa maneno.
Katika sentensi Nina kalamu mbili nyekundu, neno la namba ni lipi?
Maneno ya rangi na namba hufanya uandishi kuwa wa kuvutia.

units.title: Siku za wiki
units.notes: Wiki moja ina siku saba zinazofuatana kwa mpangilio maalum. Siku hizo ni Jumatatu, Jumanne, Jumatano, Alhamisi, Ijumaa, Jumamosi na Jumapili. Tunakwenda shule kuanzia Jumatatu hadi Ijumaa, na tunapumzika nyumbani Jumamosi pamoja na Jumapili. Kujua siku hizi hutusaidia kupanga kazi zetu na kukumbuka matukio muhimu katika shule. Tunaweza kuandika sentensi kama Tuna mchezo wa mpira Ijumaa na tunaenda kanisani yetu kila Jumapili.
units.worked_example: Ikiwa leo ni Jumatano, kesho ni Alhamisi na jana ilikuwa Jumanne.
units.activity: Taja siku saba za wiki kwa mpangilio kwa mzazi wako, na umwambie siku unayoipenda zaidi.
units.check: Siku ipi huja moja kwa moja baada ya Jumapili?

quiz.prompt: Wiki moja ina siku ngapi?
Siku ipi huja moja kwa moja baada ya Jumapili?
Tunakwenda shule kuanzia Jumatatu hadi Ijumaa.
Tunapumzika nyumbani siku zipi?
Kujua siku za wiki hutusaidia kupanga kazi zetu.

units.title: Kuuliza na kujibu maswali
units.notes: Tunauliza maswali tunapotaka kujua jambo fulani muhimu sana. Swali huanza mara nyingi na maneno kama nini, wapi, nani, lini, kwa nini au vipi. Kila swali huisha na alama ya kuuliza mwishoni. Kwa mfano, swali Mkoba wangu uko wapi huuliza kuhusu mahali kitu kilipo. Kujibu maswali kwa uwazi na heshima huonyesha kwamba tunaelewa tunachosoma na kusikia, na hii hutusaidia kujifunza kila siku.
units.worked_example: Swali: Mwalimu wako ni nani? Jibu wazi ni: Mwalimu wangu ni Bw. Otieno.
units.activity: Uliza rafiki yako maswali matatu ukitumia nini, wapi na nani, na usikilize majibu yake kwa makini.
units.check: Tunatumia alama gani mwishoni mwa swali?

quiz.prompt: Swali huisha na alama gani?
Ni neno lipi linaweza kuanza swali?
Kila swali huisha na alama ya kuuliza.
Swali Mkoba wangu uko wapi huuliza kuhusu nini?
Kujibu maswali kwa uwazi huonyesha kwamba tunaelewa.

units.title: Kusimulia hadithi
units.notes: Hadithi nzuri huwa na mwanzo, kati na mwisho wenye maana kubwa. Tunaposimulia hadithi tena, tunaeleza kilichotokea kwa mpangilio sahihi wa wakati kuanzia mwanzo hadi mwisho. Tunaweza kutumia maneno kama kwanza, kisha, baadaye na mwishowe kuonyesha mpangilio wa matukio kwa uwazi. Kusikiliza hadithi vizuri hukuza msamiati, kumbukumbu, mawazo yetu na hisia zetu. Kusimulia tena huonyesha kwamba tulielewa hadithi vyema sana na kwa makini.
units.worked_example: Simulia hadithi fupi kwa mpangilio: Kwanza sungura alikimbia kwa haraka. Kisha kobe alitembea polepole. Mwishowe kobe alishinda mbio.
units.activity: Sikiliza hadithi fupi kutoka kwa mzazi wako, kisha uisimulie kwa mtu mwingine kwa maneno yako mwenyewe.
units.check: Maneno gani matatu yanaweza kukusaidia kuonyesha mpangilio wa matukio katika hadithi?

quiz.prompt: Hadithi nzuri huwa na sehemu zipi tatu?
Maneno yapi yanaonyesha mpangilio wa matukio?
Kusimulia hadithi tena tunaeleza kilichotokea kwa mpangilio sahihi.
Kusikiliza hadithi hukuza nini?
Kusimulia tena huonyesha kwamba tulielewa hadithi vyema.

units.title: Kuandika aya fupi
units.notes: Aya ni kundi la sentensi zinazozungumzia wazo moja tu. Kila sentensi huanza na herufi kubwa na huisha na nukta mwishoni. Katika Gredi ya Tatu tunaweza kuandika sentensi tatu au nne kuhusu mada tunayoijua vyema kabisa. Kwa mfano, tunaweza kuandika kuhusu shule yetu, familia yetu au mnyama wetu wa kufuga. Kuandika kila siku hufanya mwandiko na hati zetu kuwa bora zaidi kila siku.
units.worked_example: Andika kuhusu familia yako: Ninaishi na familia yangu Thika. Baba yangu ni mkulima. Mama yangu huuza mboga. Kila sentensi imekamilika.
units.activity: Andika sentensi nne fupi kuhusu rafiki yako wa karibu na uzisome kwa sauti mbele ya darasa.
units.check: Aya fupi darasani kwako inapaswa kuwa na sentensi ngapi?

quiz.prompt: Aya ni kundi la sentensi zinazozungumzia nini?
Katika Gredi ya Tatu tunaweza kuandika sentensi ngapi?
Kila sentensi huanza na herufi kubwa na huisha na nukta.
Tunaweza kuandika kuhusu nini?
options: Shule yetu, familia yetu au mnyama wetu

quiz.prompt: Kuandika kila siku hufanya mwandiko na hati kuwa bora.

Mathematics.overview: A hands-on guide to early Mathematics for Grades 1 to 3, starting with counting and number work and moving to shapes, money, time and simple data. Examples use everyday Kenyan objects, foods and the shilling.

units.title: Counting numbers 1 to 100
units.notes: Counting helps us to know how many things there are in a group. We start from one and count forward in the correct order from small to big. We can count in ones, twos, fives and even tens. Counting in tens is quick, like ten, twenty, thirty, forty and fifty. Practise counting things around you such as stones, spoons, mangoes or goats every day.
units.worked_example: Count the ten mangoes in a row by saying one, two and three up to ten, then say there are ten mangoes.
units.activity: Collect twenty small stones and count them first in twos and then in fives.
units.check: What number comes just after thirty-nine when counting in ones?

quiz.prompt: What number comes just after thirty-nine when counting in ones?
Counting in tens gives which numbers?
options: ten, twenty, thirty, forty and fifty

quiz.prompt: Counting in tens is quicker than counting in ones.
When counting in ones we move in what order?
Counting helps us to know how many things there are in a group.

units.title: Reading and writing numbers
units.notes: We read numbers by saying their value and write them using digits. The number 67 is read as sixty-seven and written with the digits six and seven. Numbers from ten to ninety-nine have two digits. Reading and writing numbers every day helps us to work with larger amounts. Remember that the way we say a number matches the way we write it.
units.worked_example: The number fifty-two is written as 52. The number 84 is read as eighty-four.
units.activity: Write the numbers from twenty to thirty in your book and read each one aloud.
units.check: How do you write the number seventy as digits?

quiz.prompt: How do you write the number seventy as digits?
The number 67 is read as what?
Numbers from ten to ninety-nine have two digits.
The number 67 is written using which digits?
The way we say a number matches the way we write it.

units.title: Tens and ones
units.notes: Every two-digit number is made of tens and ones. In the number 34, the 3 shows three tens and the 4 shows four ones. Three tens is the same as thirty, so thirty plus four makes thirty-four. Understanding tens and ones helps us to add and subtract bigger numbers. Bundles of ten sticks are a good way to see this clearly.
units.worked_example: In the number 46, the digit 4 stands for forty and the digit 6 stands for six, so 46 is forty plus six.
units.activity: Bundle sticks in groups of ten and work out how many tens and ones there are in the number 25.
units.check: In the number 58, what does the digit 5 stand for?

quiz.prompt: In the number 34, what does the digit 3 show?
In the number 58, what does the digit 5 stand for?
Three tens is the same as thirty.
The number 34 is made of what?
Bundles of ten sticks help us see tens and ones clearly.

units.title: Adding numbers
units.notes: Addition means putting groups together to find the total. We use the plus sign when we add two or more numbers. For example, 3 + 4 = 7 means three things and four more things make seven. We can add using objects, fingers or counting on from a number. Adding becomes easy when we know our number facts well and practise every day.
units.worked_example: If you have 5 oranges and buy 3 more, you have 5 + 3 = 8 oranges.
units.activity: Use bottle tops to add two groups, for example 6 tops plus 4 tops, and write the answer.
units.check: What is 7 + 5?

quiz.prompt: What is 7 + 5?
Addition means what?
options: Putting groups together to find the total

quiz.prompt: We use the plus sign when we add.
3 + 4 = 7 means what?
options: Three things and four more make seven

quiz.prompt: We can add using objects, fingers or counting on.

units.title: Taking away numbers
units.notes: Subtraction means taking away or finding the difference between groups. We use the minus sign when we subtract one number from another. For example, 9 - 4 = 5 means if we take four away from nine, five remain. We can subtract by crossing out objects or counting backwards on a number line. Subtraction helps us to know how much is left after we take some away.
units.worked_example: A shop had 10 loaves of bread and sold 6, so there are 10 - 6 = 4 loaves left.
units.activity: Put eight stones on a desk, take away three, and count how many are left.
units.check: What is 12 - 7?

quiz.prompt: What is 12 - 7?
Subtraction means what?
options: Taking away or finding the difference

quiz.prompt: We use the minus sign when we subtract.
9 - 4 = 5 means what?
options: If we take four away from nine, five remain

quiz.prompt: We can subtract by crossing out objects or counting backwards.

units.title: Multiplication as repeated addition
units.notes: Multiplication is a fast way of adding equal groups. When we add 2 + 2 + 2, we can write it as 3 groups of 2, which is 3 x 2 = 6. The multiplication sign tells us to add equal groups. Multiplication saves time when there are many equal groups. We can see it in rows of desks or bunches of bananas.
units.worked_example: Four plates each have three chapati, so that is 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12, which is 4 x 3 = 12.
units.activity: Arrange bottle tops in four groups of five and find the total by repeated addition.
units.check: What is 5 + 5 + 5 written as a multiplication?

quiz.prompt: What is 5 + 5 + 5 written as a multiplication?
3 x 2 = 6 means what?
options: Two groups of three added to three

quiz.prompt: Multiplication is a fast way of adding equal groups.
2 + 2 + 2 can be written as what?
Multiplication saves time when there are many equal groups.

units.title: Sharing equally
units.notes: Division means sharing things equally into groups of the same size. When we share 8 sweets equally between 2 children, each child gets 4, so 8 divided by 2 equals 4. Division is the exact opposite of multiplication. We can share using real objects to see how many each person gets. Sharing fairly is also a very good lesson in kindness and honesty.
units.worked_example: Share 12 pencils equally among 4 children. Each child gets 12 divided by 4, which is 3 pencils.
units.activity: Share twenty beans equally among five plates and count how many beans are on each plate.
units.check: If you share 10 oranges equally between 2 friends, how many does each get?

quiz.prompt: If you share 10 oranges equally between 2 friends, how many does each get?
8 divided by 2 equals what?
Division is the exact opposite of multiplication.
Division means what?
options: Sharing things equally into groups of the same size

quiz.prompt: Sharing fairly is a good lesson in kindness and honesty.

units.title: Flat shapes around us
units.notes: Flat shapes have sides and corners. A triangle has three sides, a square has four equal sides, and a rectangle has four sides with two long and two short. A circle has no straight sides and no corners. We see these shapes in doors, windows, balls, books, mats and blackboards. Knowing shapes helps us to describe and draw the things around us accurately.
units.worked_example: A school flag is often a rectangle, and a ball is round like a circle.
units.activity: Draw and name a triangle, a square, a rectangle and a circle in your book.
units.check: How many sides does a triangle have?

quiz.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?
Which shape has no straight sides and no corners?
A square has four equal sides.
A rectangle has how many sides?
We can see shapes in doors, windows and balls.

units.title: Measuring length
units.notes: We measure length to know how long or how tall something is. We can use parts of our body, such as hand spans and footsteps, or tools like a ruler and a tape measure. A ruler usually measures in centimetres and millimetres. We use a metre to measure longer things like a room or a field. Measuring helps us to compare sizes accurately.
units.worked_example: A pencil may be about 15 centimetres long, and you can use a ruler to check its length.
units.activity: Use a ruler to measure the length of your exercise book and your pencil, then write the answers.
units.check: Which tool would you use to measure the length of your desk?

quiz.prompt: Which tool would you use to measure the length of your desk?
A ruler usually measures in what?
We use a metre to measure longer things like a room or a field.
Which parts of the body can we use to measure length?
Measuring helps us to compare sizes accurately.

units.title: Kenyan money
units.notes: Money is what we use to buy and sell things in the market or shop. In Kenya we use shillings and cents. Coins come in different values, such as one shilling, five shillings, ten shillings and twenty shillings. Notes have larger values like fifty, one hundred, two hundred and one thousand shillings. We add money when buying and subtract to find our change.
units.worked_example: If a pencil costs 10 shillings and you pay with a 20-shilling coin, your change is 20 - 10 = 10 shillings.
units.activity: With an adult, look at the coins at home and add up the value of any three of them.
units.check: If a book costs 30 shillings, how much change do you get from 50 shillings?

quiz.prompt: If a book costs 30 shillings, how much change do you get from 50 shillings?
In Kenya we use which money?
Notes have larger values than coins.
Which of these is a coin value in Kenya?
We add money when buying and subtract to find our change.

units.title: Telling time
units.notes: We use a clock or a watch to tell time during the day and night. The clock has numbers from one to twelve and two hands. The short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. We also use time words such as morning, afternoon, evening and night. Knowing time helps us to follow our daily programmes well and be on time.
units.worked_example: When the short hand points to three and the long hand points to twelve, the time is three o'clock.
units.activity: Draw a clock face and show the time you wake up in the morning.
units.check: What time is it when the short hand points to ten and the long hand points to twelve?

quiz.prompt: What time is it when the short hand points to ten and the long hand points to twelve?
Which hand shows the hour?
The long hand shows the minutes.
A clock has numbers from what to what?
Knowing time helps us to follow our daily programmes and be on time.

units.title: Halves and quarters
units.notes: A fraction is a part of a whole. When we cut something into two equal parts, each part is a half. When we cut it into four equal parts, each part is a quarter. We write a half as one over two and a quarter as one over four. We can see halves and quarters when we share fruit or bread.
units.worked_example: Cut one orange into two equal parts. Each part is a half of the orange.
units.activity: Fold a piece of paper into two equal parts and then into four equal parts, and colour one part each time.
units.check: If you cut a loaf of bread into four equal parts, what fraction is one part?

quiz.prompt: If you cut a loaf of bread into four equal parts, what fraction is one part?
When we cut something into two equal parts, each part is called what?
We write a half as one over two.
How many equal parts do we cut something into to get quarters?
A fraction is a part of a whole.

units.title: Collecting and showing information
units.notes: We collect information to answer questions about things around us at school and at home. We can record it using marks, pictures or a simple table. A tally chart uses small marks to count things quickly and correctly. We can then show the information using blocks or a picture graph. This helps us to see which group has the most or the least at a glance.
units.worked_example: Ask ten friends their favourite fruit, mark each answer with a stroke, and count which fruit is chosen most.
units.activity: Count how many boys and girls are in your class and draw a simple picture graph to show it.
units.check: Which fruit was chosen most if mangoes got six marks and bananas got four?

quiz.prompt: Which fruit was chosen most if mangoes got six marks and bananas got four?
A tally chart uses what to count things?
We can show information using blocks or a picture graph.
Why do we collect information?
options: To answer questions about things around us

quiz.prompt: A picture graph helps us see which group has the most or the least.

Environmental Activities.overview: This guide introduces young learners to the people, places, plants and animals around them. It builds simple habits of caring for water, food, waste and the wider environment.

units.title: My school and its surroundings
units.notes: A school has many places that we can see, name and talk about in our lessons. We see the classroom, the office, the field, the water tap and the toilets. Our school is found in a county in Kenya, near homes, shops, farms and roads. We share these places with our friends and teachers, so we must keep them clean, safe and tidy for good learning.
units.worked_example: If you stand at your classroom door, you may see the field, a water tap and the school gate.
units.activity: Walk with your class around the school and name five places that you can see.
units.check: Can you name two places found in your school?

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a place we can see in a school?
Our school is found in what?
We should keep our school places clean, safe and tidy.
Which of these is also found near a school?
We share school places with our friends and teachers.

units.title: My home and my family
units.notes: A home is where we live with our family. Our family may have a father, a mother, brothers, sisters and grandparents. At home we have a kitchen, bedrooms, a living room and a place to play. We share work at home, such as sweeping the floor, washing dishes and fetching water. We love, greet and help each other every day.
units.worked_example: At home you might help by sweeping the floor or washing the plates before dinner.
units.activity: Draw a picture of your home and say the names of the people who live with you.
units.check: Who are the people in your family?

quiz.prompt: Who may be found in a family?
options: A father, a mother, brothers, sisters and grandparents

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a room found at home?
We share work at home, such as sweeping and washing dishes.
A home is where we do what?
We should love, greet and help each other at home.

units.title: People in my school and neighbourhood
units.notes: Many people work in our school and neighbourhood to help us. In school we have teachers, the head teacher, the cook and the watchman. In our neighbourhood we may find a shopkeeper, a farmer, a nurse and a boda boda rider. Each of these people does important work for the community. We greet them, respect them and thank them for their help.
units.worked_example: The school cook prepares our lunch, and the shopkeeper sells us food and other things we need.
units.activity: Name three people who help you at school or near your home and say what each one does.
units.check: Who helps you at school every day?

quiz.prompt: Who works in our school to help us learn?
Who may we find in our neighbourhood?
options: A shopkeeper, a farmer and a nurse

quiz.prompt: Each person in the community does important work.
We should do what to people who help us?
A boda boda rider is a person we may find in the neighbourhood.

units.title: Weather and the sky each day
units.notes: The weather changes from day to day in our county. Sometimes the sky is bright and sunny, and sometimes it is cloudy and rainy. We feel hot on sunny days and cold when it rains. Weather helps farmers know the right time to plant and harvest crops. We wear warm clothes when it is cold and carry an umbrella when it rains.
units.worked_example: Before morning break, look outside and say whether the sky is sunny, cloudy or rainy.
units.activity: Keep a simple weather chart for one week and draw a sun, a cloud or rain for each day.
units.check: What kind of weather do you see today?

quiz.prompt: What can the sky be like on different days?
What do farmers learn from the weather?
options: The right time to plant and harvest

quiz.prompt: We feel hot on sunny days and cold when it rains.
What should we carry when it rains?
Weather changes from day to day in our county.

units.title: Water around us and its uses
units.notes: Water is very important for all living things. We use water for drinking, cooking, washing our bodies and cleaning our homes. We get water from rivers, wells, taps and rain. In towns near lakes, like Kisumu, people get water from the lake. We must not waste water, and we must keep it clean so that it is safe to drink.
units.worked_example: You can save water by closing the tap tightly after washing your hands.
units.activity: List three ways you use water at home and three ways you can save it.
units.check: Why must we keep our water clean?

quiz.prompt: Why must we keep our water clean?
options: So that it is safe to drink

quiz.prompt: Where can we get water from?
People near lakes like Kisumu get water from the lake.
We use water for what?
We must not waste water.

units.title: Plants in my environment
units.notes: Many kinds of plants grow around us in our county. We can see grass, trees, flowers, maize, beans and kales in our fields. Plants need water, sunlight and good soil to grow strong and healthy. We eat some plants, such as vegetables, fruits and grains like maize and rice. Trees also give us shade, firewood, medicine and clean air to breathe.
units.worked_example: If you water a bean seed in a tin of soil, after some days you will see a small green shoot.
units.activity: Plant a bean seed in a tin of soil, water it and watch it grow for one week.
units.check: What do plants need to grow well?

quiz.prompt: What do plants need to grow well?
Which of these plants can we eat?
Trees give us shade, firewood and clean air.
Which of these is a plant we can see in a field?
Plants need water to grow strong and healthy.

units.title: Animals around us
units.notes: We share our environment with many different animals. At home we may keep cows, goats, sheep, chicken, rabbits and dogs. In parks and forests we find wild animals like lions, elephants, zebras and many birds. Some animals give us food, such as milk, meat and eggs. We must treat all animals kindly and keep them safe.
units.worked_example: A cow gives us milk, which we can drink or use to make tea and yoghurt.
units.activity: Name four animals you have seen near your home and say how each one helps people.
units.check: Which animal at your home gives you milk?

quiz.prompt: Which animal at your home gives you milk?
Where can we find wild animals?
Some animals give us food such as milk, meat and eggs.
Which of these animals may we keep at home?
We must treat all animals kindly and keep them safe.

units.title: Food we eat at home and school
units.notes: We need good food to grow well, play and learn at school. We eat foods like ugali, rice, githeri, chapati, vegetables and fruits such as bananas and mangoes. These foods give our bodies energy and help us to stay healthy. It is good to eat a mix of foods and to drink clean water with our meals. We should not waste food because it is valuable.
units.worked_example: A good lunch may have ugali, green vegetables and a piece of fruit, with a cup of water.
units.activity: Talk with your family and list the foods you ate today, then draw your favourite healthy meal.
units.check: Why is it good to eat vegetables and fruits?

quiz.prompt: Why is it good to eat vegetables and fruits?
Which of these is food we can eat?
Good food helps us grow, play and learn.
What should we drink with our meals?
We should not waste food.

units.title: Keeping my body and clothes clean
units.notes: We must keep our bodies and our clothes clean every day. We wash our hands with soap and clean water before eating and after using the toilet. We brush our teeth in the morning and before we sleep at night. We also bathe, cut our nails and wear clean clothes to school. Good clean habits keep us healthy and stop us from getting sick.
units.worked_example: Before you eat your lunch, wash your hands with soap and running water for a few seconds.
units.activity: Make a small chart showing the times you wash your hands each day for one week.
units.check: When should you wash your hands?

quiz.prompt: When should you wash your hands?
options: Before eating and after using the toilet

quiz.prompt: How often should we brush our teeth?
options: In the morning and before sleep

quiz.prompt: We should wash our hands with soap and clean water.
Which of these keeps us clean?
Good clean habits keep us healthy and stop us from getting sick.

units.title: Waste and keeping the compound clean
units.notes: Every home and school makes waste each day. Waste can be paper, food remains, bottles and plastic bags. We should put all waste in a bin, not on the ground. Some waste, like fruit peels and vegetable remains, can be put in a compost pit to make manure. Keeping our compound clean keeps away rats, flies and diseases.
units.worked_example: Instead of dropping a sweet wrapper on the floor, you can keep it and put it in the dustbin.
units.activity: Pick up waste around your classroom with your friends and put it in the correct bin.
units.check: Where should we put waste?

quiz.prompt: Where should we put waste?
Some waste like fruit peels can be put where to make manure?
Keeping our compound clean keeps away rats, flies and diseases.
Which of these is waste?
We should put all waste in a bin, not on the ground.

units.title: Soil, rocks and sand
units.notes: The ground under our feet is made up of soil, rocks and sand. Soil can be black, brown or red in colour. We find rocks and sand in rivers, on roadsides and along the coast near Mombasa. Soil is important because most plants grow in it. People also use sand, stones and rocks to build houses and roads.
units.worked_example: If you dig a small hole in the garden, you can feel that the soil is soft, while a rock is hard.
units.activity: Collect a little soil, a small stone and some sand in three tins and compare their colours.
units.check: Which of these is used to build houses, soil or stones?

quiz.prompt: Which of these is used to build houses?
What colours can soil be?
Most plants grow in soil.
Where can we find rocks and sand?
options: In rivers, on roadsides and along the coast

quiz.prompt: The ground under our feet is made up of soil, rocks and sand.

units.title: Shelter and where animals live
units.notes: A shelter is a place that protects us from the sun, rain, wind and cold. People live in houses built with stones, bricks, mud or iron sheets. Animals also need shelter to stay safe and warm. Birds build nests in trees, bees live in hives and cows sleep in a shed at night. We should keep our homes clean, strong and safe for everyone.
units.worked_example: A bird collects small sticks and grass to build a nest where it lays its eggs.
units.activity: Draw two kinds of shelters, one for a person and one for an animal, and label them.
units.check: What does a bird use to build its nest?

quiz.prompt: What does a bird use to build its nest?
Where do bees live?
A shelter protects us from the sun, rain, wind and cold.
Where do cows sleep at night?
People live in houses built with stones, bricks, mud or iron sheets.

units.title: Caring for our environment
units.notes: The environment is everything around us that we can see and touch. It includes trees, animals, water, air and the soil. We should plant trees and water them so that they grow well. We should not cut trees carelessly or throw waste into rivers. We should keep our county clean, green and beautiful for everyone who lives here.
units.worked_example: If everyone in your class plants one tree, your school compound will soon have many trees.
units.activity: With your teacher, plant a small tree in the school compound and promise to water it.
units.check: Why should we plant trees?

quiz.prompt: Why should we plant trees?
options: They give us clean air and shade

quiz.prompt: What should we NOT do?
The environment includes trees, animals, water, air and soil.
We should keep our county how?
We should not cut trees carelessly.

Creative Activities.overview: This guide helps young learners explore drawing, colour, modelling, music, movement and storytelling. It uses simple local materials to build confidence, skill and imagination.

units.title: Drawing lines and shapes
units.notes: Drawing starts with simple lines and shapes. We can draw straight lines, curved lines, zigzag lines and dotted lines. We also draw shapes such as circles, squares, triangles and rectangles. We use a pencil, crayon, chalk or charcoal to draw. We can make many pictures by joining these simple lines and shapes together.
units.worked_example: You can draw a house by joining a triangle for the roof with a square for the wall.
units.activity: Draw five different lines and four shapes on a plain paper and colour them.
units.check: Which shape has three sides?

quiz.prompt: Which shape has three sides?
Which of these is a kind of line we can draw?
We can draw using a pencil, crayon, chalk or charcoal.
Which shape has no straight sides?
We can make pictures by joining simple lines and shapes.

units.title: Colours around us
units.notes: Our world is full of beautiful colours that we can see every day. We see red, blue, yellow, green, orange, black and white around us. Red, blue and yellow are called primary colours. When we mix two primary colours, we can make a new colour. For example, mixing yellow and blue makes green, like the leaves of a tree.
units.worked_example: If you mix red paint with yellow paint, you will get orange paint.
units.activity: Using crayons, draw a picture using at least three different colours.
units.check: What colour do you get when you mix red and yellow?

quiz.prompt: What colour do you get when you mix yellow and blue?
Which are called primary colours?
Mixing two primary colours can make a new colour.
Which of these is a colour we can see around us?
The world is full of beautiful colours.

units.title: Drawing things in my environment
units.notes: We can draw the many things that we see around us every day. We can draw a tree, a house, a cow, a cup, a matatu or the school gate. When we draw, we look carefully at the shape, size and colour of the thing. We draw lightly with a pencil first and then add colour with crayons. Drawing every day helps us to look at things closely.
units.worked_example: To draw a cup, first draw a small oval for the top, then draw straight lines down for the sides.
units.activity: Choose one thing near your home and draw it carefully, then colour it.
units.check: What must you look at before you draw a thing?

quiz.prompt: What must you look at before you draw a thing?
Which of these can we draw?
We draw lightly with a pencil first and then add colour with crayons.
Drawing every day helps us to do what?
We can draw things we see around us every day.

units.title: Modelling with clay and dough
units.notes: We can make many things using clay, dough or plasticine. Clay is a soft kind of soil that we can shape with our hands. We can make balls, animals, cups and small pots. First we knead the clay to make it soft, then we roll and shape it. We let our finished models dry slowly in the shade so that they do not crack.
units.worked_example: To make a clay pot, roll the clay into a ball, press your thumb in the middle, then smooth the edges.
units.activity: Use clay or dough to make one animal you know and show it to your friends.
units.check: What do we do to clay to make it soft?

quiz.prompt: What do we do to clay to make it soft?
Which of these can we make using clay?
Clay is a soft kind of soil we can shape with our hands.

We should let our models dry slowly so that they do not crack.

units.title: Making patterns
units.notes: A pattern is a design that repeats itself again and again. We can see patterns on leso cloth, baskets, mats and walls. Patterns can be made using shapes, lines and different colours. We can make a pattern by repeating a shape such as a circle, a triangle or a square. Patterns make many things in our homes look beautiful.
units.worked_example: You can draw a row of circles in red, blue, red, blue to make a simple repeating pattern.
units.activity: Cut small shapes from coloured paper and arrange them in a repeating pattern on a card.
units.check: What happens in a pattern?

quiz.prompt: What happens in a pattern?
options: A design repeats itself again and again

quiz.prompt: Where can we see patterns?
options: On leso cloth, baskets and mats

Which shape can we repeat to make a pattern?
Patterns make things in our homes look beautiful.

units.title: Paper folding and tearing
units.notes: We can make many things from paper by folding, tearing and cutting. Folding paper to make shapes is called origami. We can fold paper into a fan, a boat, a hat or an aeroplane. We can also tear small pieces of coloured paper and glue them to make a picture. We must always use paper and scissors carefully to avoid cuts.
units.worked_example: Fold a square paper in half, then fold it again to make a small triangle fan.
units.activity: Fold a paper boat or a paper aeroplane by following your teacher, then test if it floats or flies.

options: Tear and glue them to make a picture

units.title: Weaving with local materials
units.notes: Weaving means joining strips of material together to make something useful and beautiful. We can weave using paper strips, grass, sisal, banana leaves or palm leaves. People in many parts of Kenya weave baskets, mats, hats and fans. We pass one strip over and under another strip again and again. Weaving takes patience, care and very steady hands.
units.worked_example: Using two colours of paper strips, weave them over and under to make a small mat.
units.activity: Weave a simple mat using paper strips of two different colours.
units.check: What materials can we use for weaving?

quiz.prompt: What materials can we use for weaving?

options: Pass one strip over and under another

Weaving means joining strips of material to make something useful.

units.title: Singing simple songs
units.notes: Singing makes us happy and brings people together. We sing songs at school, at home and during festivals. We can sing about our country, our family or the weather. When we sing, we should breathe well, open our mouths and sing clearly. We can clap our hands or drum as we sing together.
units.worked_example: You can sing the first line of a song softly, then sing it again more loudly.
units.activity: Sing a short song you know with your friends and clap the beat together.
units.check: What can you do with your hands while singing?

options: Our country, our family or the weather

units.title: Moving to music
units.notes: We can move our bodies in different ways when we hear music or singing. We can clap our hands, stamp our feet, jump, skip and sway. Moving the body to music is also called dancing. We move slowly to slow music and quickly to fast music. Moving and dancing keep our bodies strong, active, happy and healthy.
units.worked_example: When the drum beats fast, you can jump quickly; when it beats slowly, you can sway gently.
units.activity: Play a drum or clap a beat while your friends move to the rhythm.
units.check: How do we move to slow music?

quiz.prompt: How do we move to slow music?

Moving and dancing keep our bodies strong and healthy.

We move quickly to fast music.

units.title: Telling and acting stories
units.notes: Stories are full of fun and good lessons for us. We can tell stories about animals, like the clever hare. When we act a story, we use our faces, our voices and our bodies. We can also use simple things as costumes, like a cloth or a paper mask. Acting a story helps us speak clearly and with confidence.
units.worked_example: If you act the story of the hare and the hyena, you can use a cloth as a costume and speak in different voices.
units.activity: In a small group, act out a short story you know for your class.
units.check: What can you use as a simple costume for a play?

Acting a story helps us speak clearly and with confidence.

Stories are full of fun and good lessons.

units.title: Making simple musical instruments
units.notes: We can make simple instruments using local materials. We can make shakers by filling a tin or bottle with dry beans or seeds. We can make a drum using a tin, a stick and a piece of leather or rubber. We can also make sticks to beat a rhythm. We make music together with our instruments.
units.worked_example: Put some dry beans in an empty bottle, close it well, then shake it to make a shaker sound.
units.activity: Make one shaker or drum from safe materials at home and use it to make a beat.

options: A tin, a stick and leather or rubber

We make music together with our instruments.

units.title: Building models with safe materials
units.notes: We can build small models using safe materials from around us. We can use boxes, sticks, bottle tops, clay and paper. We can build a house, a car, a bridge or a small farm. We join the parts using glue, string or sticky tape. We must be careful with sharp or broken materials so that we do not get hurt.
units.worked_example: To make a toy car, join four bottle tops as wheels to a small box using a stick for the axle.
units.activity: Build a simple model of a house or a car using safe materials and show it to your class.

Why must we be careful with sharp materials?
options: So that we do not get hurt

units.title: Decorating useful items
units.notes: We can decorate the things we use every day to make them beautiful. We can decorate a pencil holder, a greeting card, a bag or a calabash. We can use paint, coloured paper, beads or local seeds. We make neat patterns and shapes when we decorate. We must keep our work clean, tidy and attractive.
units.worked_example: You can wrap a tin with coloured paper, glue on beads and seeds, and use it as a pencil holder.
units.activity: Decorate a small box or tin at home and use it to keep your pencils or other small items.
units.check: What can you decorate to make it beautiful?

We can decorate the things we use every day.

Religious Education.overview: This guide helps young learners grow in good values such as love, honesty, kindness, fairness and respect. It uses simple stories and everyday examples from home, school and the community.

units.title: Who I am and where I belong
units.notes: Every person is special and important in the whole world. I have my own name, my family and my home. I belong to a family, a school and a community in my county. I can do many good things, like singing, drawing and helping others. I am loved, and I should also love myself and everyone around me.
units.worked_example: You can say your full name, the name of your school and the name of your county with confidence.
units.activity: Stand up and tell your friends your name, your school and one thing you are good at.
units.check: What makes every person special?

quiz.prompt: What makes every person special?
options: Having their own name, family and home

quiz.prompt: What do I belong to?
options: A family, a school and a community

quiz.prompt: I am loved, and I should love myself and everyone around me.
What good things can I do?
Every person is special and important.

units.title: My family and being thankful
units.notes: A family is a special gift from God, and we should be thankful for it. My family cares for me, feeds me, teaches me and keeps me safe. My family may have parents, brothers, sisters and grandparents. I can show my thanks by helping with small jobs at home. I should respect and love every member of my family every day.
units.worked_example: You can show thanks by helping to sweep the house or wash the dishes without being told.
units.activity: Draw your family and say one thing you thank each person for.
units.check: How can you show thanks to your family?

quiz.prompt: How can you show thanks to your family?
options: By helping with small jobs at home

quiz.prompt: A family is described as what?
My family cares for me, feeds me, teaches me and keeps me safe.
Who may be in my family?
I should respect and love every member of my family.

units.title: Caring, sharing and being kind
units.notes: Being kind means doing good things for the people around us. We can show kindness by sharing our food, our books and our toys. We can help a friend who is sad, lonely or hurt. We should speak gently, use kind words and never hurt others. Kind people make their homes, schools and friends happy.
units.worked_example: If your friend has no pencil, you can share yours and help them finish the work.
units.activity: Do one kind act for a friend or family member today and tell your class about it.
units.check: What can you share with a friend who has nothing?

quiz.prompt: What can you share with a friend who has nothing?
Being kind means doing what?
options: Good things for the people around us

quiz.prompt: We should speak gently and use kind words.
How can we help a friend who is sad?
Kind people make their homes, schools and friends happy.

units.title: Honesty and telling the truth
units.notes: We should always tell the truth to our family, teachers and friends. Telling the truth is called honesty. When we make a mistake or do something wrong, we should say sorry and tell the truth. People trust those who are honest, and they give them jobs and help. Lying makes people sad and breaks the trust between friends.
units.worked_example: If you break a cup, you should tell your parents the truth instead of hiding it.
units.activity: Tell your class about one time you told the truth and how it made you feel happy.
units.check: Why should we always tell the truth?

quiz.prompt: Why should we always tell the truth?
options: So that we get into trouble
So that people can trust us

quiz.prompt: Telling the truth is called what?
When we make a mistake we should say sorry and tell the truth.
What happens when we lie?
options: It makes people sad and breaks trust

quiz.prompt: People trust those who are honest.

units.title: Obeying parents and teachers
units.notes: Our parents and teachers guide us and keep us safe every single day. We should obey them and follow the good rules that they give us. Obeying means doing what is right, good and acceptable. When we obey, we stay safe, learn well and make our families proud. Disobeying our parents and teachers can bring trouble and danger.
units.worked_example: When your teacher asks you to sit down and keep quiet, you should obey at once.
units.activity: Make a small chart of three rules at home or school that you will obey every day.
units.check: Why should we obey our parents and teachers?

quiz.prompt: Why should we obey our parents and teachers?
options: They guide us and keep us safe

quiz.prompt: What does obeying mean?
options: Doing what is right, good and acceptable

quiz.prompt: When we obey, we stay safe, learn well and make our families proud.
What can disobeying bring?
Our parents and teachers guide us and keep us safe.

units.title: God and the beautiful world we live in
units.notes: The world we live in is full of beautiful things. We see mountains, rivers, trees, animals and bright sunshine. Many people believe that God created the world and gave us all these good things. We should take care of the world and say thank you to God. We can thank God by caring well for what we have.
units.worked_example: When you see a beautiful flower or a rainbow, you can say thank you to God for it.
units.activity: Draw a beautiful thing from nature that you have seen, such as a tree or a mountain.
units.check: What beautiful things in nature can you thank God for?

quiz.prompt: What beautiful things in nature can you thank God for?

We should take care of the world and say thank you to God.

options: By caring well for what we have

units.title: People who help us
units.notes: There are many people who help us in our daily life. Our parents, teachers, nurses, doctors, farmers and police officers all help us. Farmers grow our food, and shopkeepers sell us the things we need. We should respect these people and say thank you to them. We can also help others, because God wants us to care for one another.
units.worked_example: A nurse helps sick people to feel better, just as a teacher helps us to learn.

options: By saying thank you and respecting them

Nurses, doctors and police officers all help us.

God wants us to care for one another.

units.title: Saying sorry and forgiving
units.notes: Sometimes we may hurt our friends or family by mistake. When we do something wrong, we should say sorry and truly mean it. When someone hurts us and says sorry, we should be ready to forgive them. Forgiving means letting go of anger and being friends again. Saying sorry and forgiving bring peace to our homes, schools and hearts.
units.worked_example: If you step on your friend and hurt them, you can say sorry, and your friend can forgive you.
units.activity: Role play with a friend: one says sorry and the other forgives, then shake hands.
units.check: What should you do after you hurt a friend by mistake?

options: Say sorry and truly mean it

options: Letting go of anger and being friends again

When we do something wrong, we should say sorry.

units.title: Being polite and respectful
units.notes: Being polite means using good and kind words in every place. We say please, thank you, sorry and excuse me to everyone. We greet people when we meet them and answer them nicely. We should respect older people and help them whenever we can. Polite and respectful children are loved by everyone around them.
units.worked_example: When you ask for a pencil, you should say please, and when you get it, you should say thank you.

units.title: Working together and helping others
units.notes: We can do much more when we work together with others. Working together as a group is called teamwork. In a group we listen to one another, share ideas and share the work fairly. When we help others who need help, we show love and care. God is happy when people live together in peace and unity.
units.worked_example: If four friends each carry one chair, the work of arranging the class becomes easy and quick.
units.activity: Work in a group to clean a small part of the school compound and finish the task together.

God is happy when people live together in peace and unity.

units.title: Special days and festivals
units.notes: We all have special days that we celebrate with great joy. We celebrate birthdays, harvest days, national days and religious festivals. On these days we sing, dance, eat good food and give thanks. We celebrate with our family, friends and community. Special days help us remember important things and to be thankful.
units.worked_example: On a national day, you may sing the national anthem, watch a parade and share food with your family.
units.activity: Draw one special day you enjoy celebrating and tell your class why you like it.

options: Sing, dance, eat good food and give thanks

We celebrate special days with great joy.

units.title: Being fair to everyone
units.notes: Being fair means treating all people in the same kind and good way. We should not favour one friend and leave out another. We take turns when we play games and share things equally. Being fair also means not cheating, not bullying and not telling lies. Fair people are trusted and respected by everyone in the community.
units.worked_example: When playing a game, you can let everyone have an equal turn to play, even the shy friend.
units.activity: Play a turn-taking game with your class and make sure everyone gets a fair turn.

units.title: Caring for all living things
units.notes: All living things are important, including people, animals and plants. We should care for animals by giving them food, clean water and shelter. We should not beat, chase or hurt animals. We should also care for plants by watering them and not cutting them carelessly. Caring for all living things shows love, kindness and good character.
units.worked_example: If you keep a small bird or a dog at home, you should give it food and clean water every day.
units.activity: Water a plant or feed an animal at home each day for one week and tell the class what you did.
